Hon'ble Brij Raj Singh,J.
1. Heard Ms. Mandavi Pandey, learned counsel for the accused-applicant, Shri Anand Kumar,
Advocate holding brief of Shri Amit Kumar Awasthi, learned counsel for complainant as well as Shri
Mvs Chauhan, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. This bail application has been filed seeking release of the accused/applicant Smt. Geeta on bail,
who is involved in Case Crime No. 95 of 2023 under Sections 498A, 304-B I.P.C and Section 3/4
D.P. Act, Police Station Pisawan, District Sitapur.

3.  Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the First Information Report was lodged by the father of the deceased, wherein it is mentioned that the daughter of the complainant was married to the son of of the applicant on 08.07.2022.
As per First Information Report, the applicant, her family members and the husband of the deceased used to harass the victim/deceased and demanded a motorcycle as additional dowry.

It is further alleged that the informant got information that his Smt. Geeta vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Civil ... on 12 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191366148/
1 daughter was killed by her in-laws.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that the post-mortem report does not indicate any external or internal injury on the body of the deceased except for the ligature mark on the neck.

entities.text: Smt. Geeta vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Civil
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submitted that the deceased committed suicide by hanging herself because the relationship between the the deceased and her husband was not cordial because the deceased wanted to live separately.
Learned counsel for applicant further submitted that the applicant is a 56 years old lady (mother-in-law of the deceased) and has requested for the benefit of Section 437 Cr.P.C.

Learned counsel for applicant submitted that general allegation of dowry demand has been levelled against the applicant and she has been falsely implicated in the present case as no report was ever lodged prior to the present case and no specific role has been assigned to the applicant.

In support of his argument, learned counsel for applicant has filed the Aadhar Card of the applicant and has further stated that there is no previous criminal history of the applicant and she is languishing in jail since 27.04.2023.

5. Both learned counsel for complainant and learned A.G.A for the State have opposed the prayer of bail of the applicant and have stated that it is a case of dowry death, therefore, the applicant is not entitled for bail and her bail is liable to be rejected.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, perusing the record, also considering the nature of allegations, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, the argument that the applicant is the mother-in-law of the deceased and general allegation of dowry demand has been levelled against her, the argument that post-mortem report does not indicate any internal or external injury on the person of the deceased except for the ligature mark on the neck, the argument that the deceased committed suicide by hanging herself and the argument that the applicant is a lady and has requested for the benefit of Section 437 Cr.P.C, I find it to be a fit case for grant of bail.
7. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Smt. Geeta be released on bail in the above case crime number on her furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that she shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through her counsel.

In case of her absence, without sufficient cause,
the trial court may proceed against her under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: (iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure her presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and if the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then the trial court shall initiate proceedings against her, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against her in accordance with law.

9. It is made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The Trial Court shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions on the basis of evidence led unaffected by anything in this order.
